subproblem.title: Coordinate isomorphism ℝ × ℝ^N ≅ ℝ^{N+1}, (t, x) ↦ (t, x_1, …, x_N)
subproblem.statement: For every N ∈ ℕ there is a continuous linear equivalence L : ℝ × ℝ^N → ℝ^{N+1} with the following three properties. Here ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) = Euclid P, and ℝ × ℝ^N carries the product normed-space structure. (i) L(t, x) = (t, x_1, …, x_N), i.e. L (t, x) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x)), for all t ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^N. (ii) L(1, 0) = e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1. (iii) ‖L(0, x)‖ = ‖x‖ for every x ∈ ℝ^N.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ L : (ℝ × Euclid N) ≃L[ℝ] Euclid (N + 1), (∀ (t : ℝ) (x : Euclid N), L (t, x) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x))) ∧ L (1, 0) = EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∧ ∀ x : Euclid N, ‖L (0, x)‖ = ‖x‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 (Coordinates) of the parent proof, packaged as one continuous linear equivalence. Fix N.
1. Linear equivalence. Let e : ℝ × ℝ^N ≃ₗ[ℝ] ℝ^{N+1} be the composite (LinearEquiv.trans) of three linear equivalences:
 (a) (LinearEquiv.refl ℝ ℝ).prodCongr (WithLp.linearEquiv 2 ℝ (Fin N → ℝ)), which sends (t, x) to (t, WithLp.ofLp x);
 (b) Fin.consLinearEquiv ℝ (fun _ : Fin (N + 1) => ℝ), which sends (t, y) to Fin.cons t y;
 (c) (WithLp.linearEquiv 2 ℝ (Fin (N + 1) → ℝ)).symm, which sends z to WithLp.toLp 2 z.
 Unfolding the three maps gives e (t, x) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x)) for all t and x; this is a definitional equality, closed by rfl.
2. Continuity. ℝ × ℝ^N is finite-dimensional, and both sides are Hausdorff topological vector spaces over the complete field ℝ. So L := e.toContinuousLinearEquiv (LinearEquiv.toContinuousLinearEquiv) is a continuous linear equivalence with the same underlying function. By step 1 this proves (i).
3. Property (ii). By (i), L (1, 0) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons 1 (WithLp.ofLp 0)). Two points of ℝ^{N+1} are equal when all their coordinates agree; split the index with Fin.cases.
 - At index 0 the left side is Fin.cons 1 _ 0 = 1, and EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 also has coordinate 1 there.
 - At index j.succ the left side is (WithLp.ofLp 0) j = 0, and single 0 1 has coordinate 0 there because j.succ ≠ 0 (Fin.succ_ne_zero).
 Hence L (1, 0) = EuclideanSpace.single 0 1.
4. Property (iii). By (i) and EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, ‖L (0, x)‖ = √(Σ_{i : Fin (N+1)} ‖Fin.cons 0 (WithLp.ofLp x) i‖²). Split the sum with Fin.sum_univ_succ and use Fin.cons_zero and Fin.cons_succ: the sum becomes ‖0‖² + Σ_{j : Fin N} ‖x_j‖² = Σ_j ‖x_j‖². Its square root is ‖x‖ by EuclideanSpace.norm_eq again (simp closes the goal).
5. Steps 2–4 give a continuous linear equivalence L with (i), (ii) and (iii). □
proof_key_steps: Compose (refl × WithLp.linearEquiv), Fin.consLinearEquiv and (WithLp.linearEquiv).symm into a linear equivalence e with e(t, x) = toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (ofLp x)) by rfl.
Finite dimension upgrades e to a continuous linear equivalence L (LinearEquiv.toContinuousLinearEquiv), which gives (i).
L(1, 0) = EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 by comparing coordinates with Fin.cases and Fin.succ_ne_zero.
‖L(0, x)‖ = ‖x‖ by EuclideanSpace.norm_eq and Fin.sum_univ_succ.

subproblem.title: Part (e): integral bound for the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors
subproblem.statement: Let N, k ∈ ℕ, α a k-covector on ℝ^N (α : Covector (Euclid N) k), f : ℝ → Λ^k(ℝ^N)* continuous, and c ∈ ℝ. Assume α(v) = ∫_0^1 f(t)(v) dt for all v ∈ (ℝ^N)^k, and covectorEuclideanNorm (f t) ≤ c for all t ∈ [0, 1]. Then covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ c. Here covectorEuclideanNorm is SimonGMT's Euclidean coefficient norm √(Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e_{I_1}, …, e_{I_k})²).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N k : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid N) k) (f : ℝ → Covector (Euclid N) k) (c : ℝ), Continuous f → (∀ v : Fin k → Euclid N, α v = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, f t v) → (∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, covectorEuclideanNorm (f t) ≤ c) → covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ c
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 8 (Minkowski's integral inequality for the Euclidean coefficient norm of Simon 6.1.15). Fix N, k, α, f, c with f continuous and the hypotheses (H1) α(v) = ∫_0^1 f(t)(v) dt for all v, and (H2) covectorEuclideanNorm (f t) ≤ c for t ∈ [0, 1]. Let e := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin N) ℝ, and for I : Fin k → Fin N let e_I := (i ↦ e (I i)).
1. Coefficient vector. Define κ : Λ^k(ℝ^N)* → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k → Fin N) by κ(γ) := WithLp.toLp 2 (I ↦ if StrictMono I then γ(e_I) else 0).
2. Norm identity. For every γ, ‖κ(γ)‖ = covectorEuclideanNorm γ. Indeed, EuclideanSpace.norm_eq gives ‖κ(γ)‖ = √(Σ_I ‖κ(γ)_I‖²). By cases on StrictMono I, each term ‖κ(γ)_I‖² equals (if StrictMono I then γ(e_I)² else 0). The result is exactly the sum under the square root in the definition of covectorEuclideanNorm.
3. Continuity. κ is WithLp.toLp (PiLp.continuous_toLp) applied to a map that is continuous coordinatewise (continuous_pi). Each coordinate is either evaluation at e_I (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid N) ℝ e_I, which is continuous linear) or the constant 0. So κ is continuous, and t ↦ κ(f t) is continuous, hence interval integrable on [0, 1].
4. κ(α) = ∫_0^1 κ(f t) dt. Compare coordinates I (ext). The projection EuclideanSpace.proj I is continuous linear and commutes with the interval integral (ContinuousLinearMap.intervalIntegral_comp_comm), so (∫_0^1 κ(f t) dt)_I = ∫_0^1 κ(f t)_I dt. If StrictMono I, this is ∫_0^1 f(t)(e_I) dt = α(e_I) = κ(α)_I, by (H1) with v = e_I. Otherwise both sides are 0, since the integral of 0 is 0.
5. Estimate. For t ∈ Ι 0 1 = Ioc 0 1 ⊆ Icc 0 1 (uIoc_of_le zero_le_one), step 2 and (H2) give ‖κ(f t)‖ = covectorEuclideanNorm (f t) ≤ c. By intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const, ‖∫_0^1 κ(f t) dt‖ ≤ c · |1 − 0| = c. Hence, by steps 2 and 4, covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖κ(α)‖ = ‖∫_0^1 κ(f t) dt‖ ≤ c. □
proof_key_steps: Define the coefficient map κ(γ) := toLp (I ↦ [StrictMono I]·γ(e_I)); then ‖κ(γ)‖ = covectorEuclideanNorm γ by EuclideanSpace.norm_eq.
κ is continuous, so t ↦ κ(f t) is interval integrable.
Coordinatewise (EuclideanSpace.proj, intervalIntegral_comp_comm) and by the hypothesis, κ(α) = ∫_0^1 κ(f t) dt.
intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const gives ‖κ(α)‖ ≤ c·|1 − 0| = c.

Continuity and coordinatewise integration establish its integral identity, and the unit-interval norm estimate proves the bound without an omitted positivity or dimensional assumption.

subproblem.title: Smoothness and derivative of parametric integrals over [0, 1]
subproblem.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, let V be a complete real normed space (V : Type), and let h : ℝ × ℝ^N → V be C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ∞, written ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)), where ℝ^N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N). Source: parent proof step 6, (c1)–(c5) (Simon 6.2.19/2.21 at the level of forms: S_{dβ} = i_1^#β − i_0^#β − dS_β). Fix N, k, β, θ satisfying the hypothesis (H): θ̃(x')(u) = ∫_0^1 β̃(ι(t, x'))(e₀, Ju) dt for all x' and u ∈ (ℝ^N)^k, where β̃ := (β : DifferentialForm) and θ̃ := (θ : DifferentialForm). Fix x and v ∈ (ℝ^N)^{k+1}. β̃ and θ̃ are C^∞ because they are test forms (β.property.1.1, θ.property.1.1), hence differentiable.
1. Pointwise split. By sibling extderiv_split (Submission.cmcdt_lpo_slice_extDeriv_split N k β̃ applied to the differentiability of β̃), for every t:
 dβ̃(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv) = deriv φ t − Σ_{j : Fin (k+1)} (−1)^j • D[x' ↦ β̃(ι(t, x'))(e₀, J(removeNth j v))](x)(v_j),

2. Coordinates. By sibling coords (Submission.cmcdt_lpo_slice_coords N), take L with L(s, y) = ι(s, y) and L(1, 0) = e₀, and rewrite (H) and the goal right-to-left with these identities. For u ∈ (ℝ^N)^k and p ∈ ℝ × ℝ^N put H_u(p) := β̃(L p)(Fin.cons L(1, 0) (i ↦ L(0, u_i))). H_u is C^∞: it is β̃ ∘ L followed by evaluation at a fixed tuple (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply), a continuous linear map. By (H), (x' ↦ θ̃(x')(u)) = (x' ↦ ∫_0^1 H_u(t, x') dt) as functions (funext).

4. Continuity in t. x' ↦ (t, x') has derivative ι₂ := ContinuousLinearMap.inr ℝ ℝ (Euclid N), so by the chain rule D_u(t) = (fderiv ℝ H_u (t, x)).comp ι₂. fderiv ℝ H_u is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv), and A ↦ A.comp ι₂ is continuous linear ((ContinuousLinearMap.compL ℝ _ _ ℝ).flip ι₂). So t ↦ D_u(t) is continuous, hence interval integrable, and ContinuousLinearMap.intervalIntegral_apply gives (∫_0^1 D_u(t) dt)(w) = ∫_0^1 D_u(t)(w) dt for every w.
5. dθ̃. By exteriorDerivative_apply (θ̃ is differentiable at x), dθ̃(x)(v) = Σ_j (−1)^j • fderiv ℝ (x' ↦ θ̃(x')(removeNth j v)) x (v_j). By steps 3 and 4 this equals Σ_j (−1)^j • ∫_0^1 D_{removeNth j v}(t)(v_j) dt. After the rewriting of step 2, D_{removeNth j v}(t)(v_j) is by definition of H exactly the j-th summand of step 1, D[x' ↦ β̃(L(t, x'))(Fin.cons L(1, 0) (i ↦ L(0, (removeNth j v) i)))](x)(v_j).
6. Fundamental theorem of calculus. φ(s) = β̃(L(s, x))(i ↦ L(0, v_i)) is C^∞, as evaluation at a fixed tuple composed with β̃, L and s ↦ (s, x). So φ is differentiable and deriv φ is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_deriv). By intervalIntegral.integral_deriv_eq_sub, ∫_0^1 deriv φ t dt = φ(1) − φ(0).
7. Integration. Each summand t ↦ (−1)^j • D_{removeNth j v}(t)(v_j) is continuous by step 4 (Continuous.clm_apply, Continuous.const_smul), so the finite sum is continuous (continuous_finsetSum), and deriv φ is continuous.  By step 5 the right-hand side is φ(1) − φ(0) − dθ̃(x)(v). Finally φ(1) = β̃(ι(1, x))(Jv) and φ(0) = β̃(ι(0, x))(Jv), which is (c). □
